evidence: Cato Agr. 156: coquitō ūsque dōnec conmadēbit bene, aquam dēfunditō
Cato Agr. 157: ubi cocta erit bene, aquam dēfunditō
terms.comment: Cato’s word for pouring the water off cooked cabbage: the cook’s “drain it”. Horace uses it of wine poured out of the jar (Lewis & Short). Through a colander, per cōlum: see “colander” and “strain”.

phrases.latin: Ubi cocta erit bene, aquam dēfunditō.
phrases.english: When it is well cooked, pour off the water.
Then pour off the water, but not all of it.

phrases.latin: Aquam per cōlum dēfunde; cavē, fervet!
phrases.english: Pour the water off through the colander; careful, it’s boiling!

sources: Lewis & Short: defundo · Lewis & Short: colum
